name: La Barranca cemetery memorial, Lardero (La Rioja)
story: La Rioja, like Navarre, fell to the rebels without a fight in July 1936, yet around two thousand people were killed in the rearguard repression in the following months. La Barranca, on the outskirts of Lardero near Logroño, was one of the main execution and burial sites: the official heritage declaration records 407 people buried here in three mass graves, killed between 10 September and 15 December 1936. Relatives' association La Barranca turned the site into a memorial cemetery; it is the principal place of remembrance for the victims of repression in La Rioja.
see: A small walled memorial cemetery with name plaques and flowers left by relatives.
plan: Outside Lardero, a short drive from Logroño (the site is also called Barrigüelo); free, open air.
